findings.question: Is adoption gated on version match AND envelope-digest match of what THIS client flushed?
findings.evidence: src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:1061-1092 `adoptFlushedRevision`: `if (record.version !== flushed.baseVersion + 1) return false;` then `if (flushedEnvelopeDigest(record) !== flushed.envelopeDigest) return false;` -- both must pass before `applySavedRecord`. `flushed` is captured at flush time (`:1035-1039`) from the envelope actually sent.

findings.question: THE CRITICAL CHECK -- does the server rewrite `savedAt`, which would make the digest never match and the fix dead code?
findings.verdict: PASS -- the server does NOT pin or rewrite savedAt. The fix is live, not dead.
findings.evidence: src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:354-407 `prepareCampaignWrite` returns `{...incoming.record, instanceId, authority}` on every branch -- it overwrites EXACTLY the three fields the digest excludes and nothing else. src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:118-155 `saveCampaign` then overwrites only `version` (`{...prepared.record, version: nextVersion}`) before `JSON.stringify(stored)` into the payload column. `savedAt` rides through from the client envelope (minted at src/lib/campaign/persistence/campaignEnvelope.ts:46, `new Date().toISOString()` per build). Independently corroborated by the measured browser case (c) = 200: a digest that could never match would leave case (c) at 409.
findings.safetyOfIncludingSavedAt: Safe and load-bearing. It is the field that makes the digest identify THIS write rather than any state that merely looks like ours. The residual the author already states -- a different writer sending a byte-identical envelope with the same millisecond savedAt would also match -- is harmless because the stored state is then identical either way.

findings.question: Does the exclusion set exactly match what the server pins?
findings.evidence: Excluded: `version`, `instanceId`, `authority` (:307-315 comment + :316-325 body). Pinned by the server: `instanceId` and `authority` (prepareCampaignWrite, all three branches) and `version` (saveCampaign:132-135). Exact correspondence -- no over-exclusion (which would weaken the check) and no under-exclusion (which would break it).

findings.question: Does `dirty` stay true after adoption, and does exactly one ordinary save follow?
findings.evidence: `applySavedRecord` sets `dirty:false` (:618-638) and `adoptFlushedRevision` immediately restores `set({ dirty: true })` (:1085). `armAutoSaveTimer` is called exactly once, in the reconciliation's single `.then` (:1144-1149), and `armAutoSaveTimer` itself clears before arming (:964-966). jsdom row 'adopts the revision the flush provably earned' asserts dirty===true after adoption, then exactly 2 PUTs total with `putBaseVersion(puts[1]) === BASE_VERSION + 1`.
findings.caveat: If the reconciliation READ outlives the 2 s debounce AND a markDirty landed during it, the mutation's own timer can fire first (it correctly awaits `inFlightLoad` and so uses the adopted token, so it is not stale), and the reconciliation then arms a SECOND timer -> one redundant no-op PUT. Harmless (no data loss, no conflict) but it breaks 'exactly one' in that window. Narrow: requires a >2 s read.

findings.question: Is the armed timer cleared before the read?
findings.evidence: :1137 `clearAutoSaveTimer();` is executed synchronously before `adoptFlushedRevision` is called at :1138. The discard-path/timer mutual-exclusion invariant of the base requirement is preserved, and the mutation-armed stale-token save is taken over rather than raced (jsdom row 'adopts the earned revision even when a mutation arrived after the flush').

findings.question: Are the failure paths byte-identical to today?
findings.verdict: PASS on state, FAIL on the literal wording
findings.evidence: On every failure branch (read throws / !response.ok / wrong version / digest mismatch) `adoptFlushedRevision` returns false having called no setter, and the reconciliation arms the ordinary save on the untouched `baseVersion` -- state-identical to pre-C2. TWO observable deltas remain: (a) a GET is now issued that was not issued before, and (b) the save is armed one round trip later than before. Both are disclosed (store docstring :1106-1113 and the C2 evidence nonClaim 'a round trip wide rather than zero'), so this is a wording looseness in the commit message, not a hidden change.

findings.question: Spec conformance -- 'An unread flush never claims a revision it did not earn'.
findings.evidence: spec.md:~168-172. The revision is recorded only after an authoritative GET proves the row is the one this client wrote; `fireKeepaliveFlush` (:942-957) is byte-identical to base -- still unread, no applySavedRecord, no baseVersion advance. The base version advances on the strength of a READ, never of having fired.
findings.cosmeticNote: Between adoption and the reconciled save the store is transiently `saveState:'saved'` AND `dirty:true`. The 'Unsaved changes' badge keys off `dirty` (CampaignSaveStatusCard.tsx:111-115), so the user-visible pending signal is correctly retained; only the small status badge reads 'Saved' alongside it. Cosmetic, non-blocking.

findings.question: Spec conformance -- 'A hidden transition the document survives still reaches an acknowledged save'.
findings.evidence: spec.md:~178-182 demands an ordinary ACKNOWLEDGED save and no pending mutations with no write scheduled. Pre-C2 only the scheduling half held (the save was refused 409 -- finding F1, measured). Post-C2 the reconciled PUT carries N+1 and measured 200 in a real browser (case (c)), with 'Unsaved changes' and 'Save refused' both asserted hidden afterwards.
findings.guardsUnchanged: co-op (isCoopCampaign), legacyUnadopted and saveState==='conflict' short-circuit BEFORE any read is issued (:1126-1135). The PUT route and its CAS are untouched (confirmed: the stack's cumulative diff names no file under src/pages/api or src/services).

findings.question: Is publishing the read as `inFlightLoad` safe against a concurrent runSave?
findings.evidence: `runSave` awaits `inFlightLoad` before it reads `get().baseVersion` (:699-701, then :715). The reconciliation assigns `inFlightLoad = reconciliation` SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the visibilitychange handler (:1153), so any save that starts afterwards blocks on it. The `.finally` clears it under an identity check (:1154-1158), the same shape `loadCampaignAction` uses (:778-783), so a concurrent load's assignment is not clobbered.
findings.residual: A save ALREADY past its `inFlightLoad` await when the reconciliation starts is not blocked. Reaching that needs an explicit `saveCampaign()` (Save-now) in flight across a hidden->visible transition; the debounced path cannot be there because the flush cleared its timer. Narrow, and the worst outcome is a stale-token 409 -- the pre-existing behaviour.

findings.question: Can a concurrent runLoad interleave badly with the reconciliation?
findings.residual: R-1 below: a `loadCampaign` that starts during the reconciliation read and resolves FIRST at a newer revision (N+2, written by another device) can be overwritten by the reconciliation's `applySavedRecord(N+1)`, downgrading `baseVersion`. Consequence is a 409 on the next save -- a conflict banner, never a silent overwrite, because the strict CAS is what catches it. Reachability is low (a route mount coinciding with a tab return).

findings.question: Can a markDirty during the read lose the adoption or double-save?
findings.evidence: markDirty (:1166-1180) sets dirty and re-arms; the reconciliation's `.then` then clears and re-arms once more, so exactly one timer survives, and `set({dirty:true})` after `applySavedRecord` means the mutation's dirty flag cannot be erased by the adoption. The live campaign is NOT overwritten by adoption -- `applySavedRecord` sets only `lastPersistedCampaign`, never `writeLiveCampaign` (contrast `rollbackCoopCampaign` at :641-665, which does) -- so a post-flush mutation in memory survives intact.
findings.onlyCaveat: the >2 s-read double-timer window in A1.4.

findings.question: Does the single-slot `issuedFlush` hold across a double flush?
findings.measured: `issuedFlush` is OVERWRITTEN on every flush (:1035-1039), while `pendingFlushIssued` is reset to false by markDirty (:1169). So the sequence [visibilitychange hidden -> flush1 lands, server N->N+1] -> [markDirty while hidden, e.g. a background/cron mutation] -> [pagehide -> flush2 fires on the SAME stale baseVersion N, server refuses 409 unread] -> [document survives, visible] leaves `issuedFlush` describing flush2 while the server row carries flush1's bytes. Version matches (N+1) but the digest does not -> no adoption -> the ordinary save goes out on N -> 409 'Save refused', i.e. the exact F1 symptom C2 exists to remove, re-reachable in this one sequence.
findings.severity: low -- requires a mutation between two discard events in one hidden episode; not reachable by an ordinary tab switch, which is the case F1 was filed for and which is fixed.
findings.notBlocking: the outcome is a conflict banner, not data loss, and it is the pre-C2 behaviour rather than a new failure mode.

axes.name: Digest helper choice and production-shape stability

findings.question: Is `toCanonicalJson` + `sha256Sync` (rather than the journal's strict JCS canonicalizer) the right choice?
findings.verdict: PASS -- justified, and the stated reason checks out
findings.evidence: src/utils/events/hashUtils.ts:20-36 `toCanonicalJson` is `JSON.stringify(obj, sortingReplacer)`. Because it IS JSON.stringify, an `undefined`-valued key is absent on both sides of the round trip. The journal's JCS encoder rejects `undefined` outright, and `serializeCampaign` emits `undefined` for absent optionals (campaignStartDate, dailyBattleAudit, loans, and the whole W3.1 optional tail at src/lib/campaign/persistence/serializeCampaign.ts:155-198), so JCS would in fact throw on the discard path as the comment claims.

findings.question: Can any field serialize differently pre-wire vs after the SQLite round trip (Money.toJSON, Map entries, Date), making the digest mismatch in production even when the flush landed?
findings.verdict: NO -- stable by construction, for two independent reasons
findings.reason1_serializerAlreadyFlattens: `serializeCampaign` (src/lib/campaign/persistence/serializeCampaign.ts:126-200) is explicitly a JSON-safe projection: Maps become `Array.from(...entries())` (forces, missions), Dates become ISO strings (currentDate, campaignStartDate), and `serializeFinances` (:45-76) flattens EVERY Money to `.amount` and every loan Date to ISO. No Money, Date or Map instance is present in `envelope.body` at digest time. `Money.toJSON` (src/types/campaign/Money.ts:113-115) is therefore never even reached on this path.
findings.reason2_fixedPoint: Even if one were present, JSON.stringify applies `toJSON` BEFORE the replacer (ES SerializeJSONProperty step order), so the pre-wire digest sees exactly the value the post-round-trip digest sees. Generally: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` is a fixed point of JSON.stringify, and the sorting replacer is deterministic on plain data (Object.keys().sort() is the same UTF-16 order on both sides), so digest(x) === digest(roundTrip(x)) for ANY x -- including NaN/Infinity->null, functions/symbols dropped, and sparse-array holes->null.
findings.serverSideNoOp: The server does not perturb `body`: `hydrateCampaignRecord` (src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAuthorityHydrate.ts:34-61) runs `migrateSerializedCampaign`, whose ladder (src/lib/campaign/persistence/campaignMigration.ts:53-64) has steps only for fromVersion 0 and 1 while `buildSerializedCampaign` always stamps `CURRENT_CAMPAIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` -- so the ladder is an identity for any client write. GET returns the hydrated stored record verbatim (`parseStoredCampaignRow` :316-336).
findings.clientSideMigrateIsAlsoNoOp: `migrateClientRecord` (:514-516) calls the same ladder, likewise identity at v2.

findings.question: Does the browser case (c) 200 prove the production shape matches?
findings.verdict: YES, and it is the right corroboration -- but it is corroboration, not the proof
findings.reasoning: Case (c) exercises a real production build, a real serializeCampaign over a real campaign with a roster projection, the real SQLite payload column and the real GET handler, and the reconciled PUT measured 200 where it measured 409 before the fix -- which is only reachable through a digest match. That is a genuine end-to-end positive. It is however ONE campaign shape (freshly seeded + advance-day), so it does not by itself cover Money/Map/optional-undefined-heavy campaigns; A3.1/A3.2's construction argument is what covers those, and the jsdom rows additionally pass the envelope through a real `JSON.stringify` -> `JSON.parse` round trip (`parsePutBody`/`storedFromFlush`) before recomputing the digest.

findings.question: Any latent fragility in the digest coupling?
findings.note: The digest assumes the server does not migrate an incoming envelope. That holds because the client always writes at CURRENT schema. If a future schema bump ever ships a server ahead of a client, the ladder would run on the incoming envelope and every digest would mismatch -- the fix would silently revert to today's 409 behaviour rather than misfire. Degrades safe, worth one sentence in the store docstring if the team ever ships mixed versions.

findings.question: Is dropping `expect(puts).toHaveLength(1)` from case (a) compensated by the version+1 assertion?

nonBlockingNotes.title: A concurrent runLoad can be undone by the reconciliation's adoption
nonBlockingNotes.detail: If `loadCampaign` starts during the reconciliation read and resolves FIRST at a newer revision written elsewhere (N+2), the reconciliation's later `applySavedRecord(N+1)` downgrades `baseVersion` and `metadata`. The strict CAS turns the next save into a 409 rather than an overwrite, so the failure mode is a conflict banner, not data loss. Reachability is low (a dashboard route mount coinciding with a tab return). If it is ever worth closing, the cheapest guard is to re-check `inFlightLoad === reconciliation` (or that `get().baseVersion` is still `flushed.baseVersion`) immediately before `applySavedRecord`.

nonBlockingNotes.title: Single-slot `issuedFlush` lets the F1 symptom re-emerge after a double flush
nonBlockingNotes.detail: See A2.4. Sequence: hidden-flush lands; a mutation occurs while hidden (clearing `pendingFlushIssued` but not `issuedFlush`); pagehide fires a second flush on the same stale token, which the server refuses; the document then survives. The read finds the FIRST flush's bytes at N+1, the digest records the SECOND's, so nothing is adopted and the reconciled save is refused 409. Narrow, not a regression (it is the pre-C2 behaviour), and safe (conflict, never overwrite).

nonBlockingNotes.title: A >2 s reconciliation read can produce one redundant no-op PUT
nonBlockingNotes.detail: See A1.4. Requires a markDirty during a read that outlives the 2 s debounce. No data loss and no conflict; it simply breaks the 'exactly one save follows' phrasing in that window.
